solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slug in newspaper

parts.note: a slug is slang for a bullet, as in a slug from a gun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sluggish garden pest turns up among the pages of the morning paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A news sheet issued regularly, such as an organisation's newsletter, is a bulletin.

clue.text: Bishop with hot drink

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
hot in the sense of lustful, which is randy

explanation.surface: A churchman takes a warming beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled spirit, an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: A bolt from the blue

parts.note: the idiom for a sudden surprise read literally: a flash striking down out of the sky

explanation.surface: An idiom for something wholly unexpected.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal thunderbolt out of a blue sky is the electrical discharge of a storm.

clue.text: Throws out broken items

indicators.note: the word items is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone discards things that no longer work.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, a synonym of throwing out.

clue.text: Insignificant people in parties

parts.note: taken as written
a sect is a faction or party within a larger group

explanation.surface: Nobodies turn up at social gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling people insects is a figurative slight: tiny, contemptible creatures of no account.

clue.text: Dance band oddly released sentimental song

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: the odd letters of band are let go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A group plays a slushy number at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad in pop usage is a slow, romantic song.

clue.text: A Teddy boy on outside of paper is drawn

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the Teddy boy's letters sit around the paper's letters

parts.note: a Ted is short for a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress
a tract is a short pamphlet or paper

explanation.surface: A 1950s youth is sketched on the cover of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a British 1950s youth in Edwardian-style suits. 'is' is a link, so the definition is just 'drawn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drawn to something means being pulled towards it, which is being attracted.

clue.text: Cover the inside with new fabric

parts.note: to line something is to cover its inner surface

explanation.surface: An upholsterer relines something with fresh material.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is cloth woven from flax, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Corrupt head of Chemotherapy in unproductive hospital department

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the word for unproductive

parts.note: dead as in a dead end or dead asset: producing nothing

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A cancer treatment stalls in a failing hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means morally decayed, a sense close to corrupt.

clue.text: Most irritated rook that is in distress

indicators.note: these letters go inside the word for distress

parts.note: angst is anxiety or distress
R is the chess notation abbreviation for rook
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A chess piece is the cause of a player's fury and distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Angriest is the superlative of angry, meaning most annoyed or vexed.

clue.text: Worried the mostly pleasant folk

indicators.note: worried as in worried at, pulled about, so the letters are reshuffled
most of the word, the final letter dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Someone frets that the pleasant mood is mostly gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' turns THE into ETH; 'mostly' trims NICE to NIC. 'folk' is adjectival, as in folk music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic music or dress is traditional to a people, the same sense as folk art.

clue.text: Piece of cake — second bite

parts.note: a nip is a small bite

explanation.surface: Someone takes a second bite of a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece of cake is an idiom for an easy task; a snip is slang for a bargain or something easy.

clue.text: Sees fruit

definitions.meaning: sees in the sense of goes out with romantically
the sweet fruit of a palm tree

explanation.surface: Someone spots some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To date someone is to see them romantically; the palm's sweet brown fruit is also called by this name.

clue.text: Prisoner prepared with no right to be held

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: the letter for right is removed

parts.note: trained means made ready, prepared

explanation.surface: A convict, rehabilitated but stripped of his rights, is kept locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the usual abbreviation for right; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contained is held within, enclosed or kept in.

clue.text: River fish rise regularly — those on a hunt?

parts.note: R abbreviates river on maps
the ide is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: every other letter of rise is taken

explanation.surface: Fish in a river surface at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox hunt is followed by people on horseback, who are riders; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: Exit scene, upset? That's life

indicators.note: the letters of exit scene are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor storms off stage in distress, musing that such is life.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence means being alive, a synonym for life.

clue.text: Pound with new shape

parts.note: to patter is to beat or tap repeatedly, as rain pounds

explanation.surface: Someone beats metal into a fresh form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a design or form, so it can stand for shape.

clue.text: Swapped old coins with old penny

parts.note: ex means former or old
loose coins are change
D, from Latin denarius, was the symbol for the pre-decimal British penny

explanation.surface: A collector trades obsolete coins plus an old penny.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for the penny in Britain's pre-1971 pounds, shillings and pence. 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange things is to trade one for another, which is swapping.

clue.text: Naughty bear cub beginning to eat grilled meat

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of bear cub run wild
only the opening letter of eat is taken

explanation.surface: A mischievous young bear starts tucking into a sizzling cookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is food cooked over an open grill, such as chargrilled meat.

clue.text: Gun has gone off one's in pain

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
gone off as in exploded, so the letters of gun has are scattered

parts.note: one's read as one is; one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A firearm has discharged and someone is hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone off' turns GUN HAS into ANGUSH; 'one's in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, a strong word for pain.

clue.text: What turns up with this paper? A number of sheets fastened together

definitions.text: A number of sheets fastened together

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what?
FT is the Financial Times, the paper printing this crossword

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks what arrives with the newspaper: a bundle of pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this paper' is the Financial Times, so FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A heft, borrowed from German, is an instalment or booklet: a sheaf of pages stitched as one part of a publication.

clue.text: Prepare wine and serve

parts.note: red is red wine
to act is to serve in a role, as in act as host

explanation.surface: A host gets the claret ready and pours it.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to edit text and make it ready for publication, so to prepare it.

clue.text: Release scoundrel I eventually imprisoned

indicators.note: the letters are locked up inside the run of words scoundrel I eventually

explanation.surface: A rogue confesses he was eventually jailed, and begs to be let out.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a duty or a burden is to free them, a sense of release.

clue.text: Cold became less severe and stopped

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
eased means lessened, became less severe

explanation.surface: A cold snap relents and finally ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased means came to an end, a synonym of stopped.

clue.text: Pretty bad failure, but right to be brushed aside

indicators.note: bad suggests something spoilt, so these letters are rearranged
the letter for right is swept out of the mix

explanation.surface: A rather poor flop, but correctness gets ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty bad' looks like 'rather poor'; 'Pretty' is the definition. 'bad' mixes FAILURE BUT less R, removed by 'to be brushed aside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beautiful and pretty are near-synonyms for attractive.

clue.text: Strength when fixed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
set means fixed in place

explanation.surface: Something becomes robust once it is mended.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality, a strong point or strength.

clue.text: Picture I framed — good for daughter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: good comes in for, replacing, daughter

parts.note: framed as in made, constructed
D abbreviates daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: An artist hangs a picture after framing it, but swaps in his daughter's good one.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Child is small and used to be ignored on a regular basis

parts.note: taken as written
S abbreviates small, as in clothing sizes

indicators.text: to be ignored on a regular basis
indicators.note: every other letter of used is skipped

explanation.surface: A little one is routinely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in legal language means offspring, so a child.

clue.text: A coin's lost here? You bet!

definitions.text: A coin's lost here? You bet!

indicators.note: lost as in gone astray, so the letters of a coin's wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler asks whether money vanishes in this place, and answers: certainly!
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house is where coins are staked and lost on wagers.

clue.text: Perhaps emails philosopher in confusion

indicators.note: the thinker is placed inside the word for confusion

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion
a sage is a wise thinker or philosopher

explanation.surface: A muddled thinker possibly sends emails.
explanation.definitionFit: Emails are one kind of communication sent to someone, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Judge bumps into rear of garage when reversing

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter
the word for bumps into is read backwards

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them by chance

explanation.surface: A judge backs his car into the back of a garage.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to regard or consider, as in judging something worthy.

clue.text: Deputy stopped and rested

parts.note: ended means stopped or finished

explanation.surface: A second-in-command halted and took a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rests on another thing when it is reliant on it, so depended.
